message.content: Work GitHub issue #36 in this repo using the /hq-work workflow (read AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md). Claim with `./hq claim 36 --agent claude`, build strictly inside the issue's Scope, run `./hq check`, rebase on origin/main, open the PR with `./hq pr 36 --body-file .context/pr-36.md`, then stop and report PR number and evidence. Do not ship/merge. Run the anti-slop skill on changed UI. For steps needing a device or keys, write code/mocked tests and say what is left for a human. Never read .env files.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: hq-work
3	description: 'Use when a human assigns you a GitHub issue ("work on #N" or "/hq-work N"). Takes it from claim to a reviewed PR.'
4	---
5	
6	# hq-work
7	
8	`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.
9	
10	1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
11	   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
12	2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
13	   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
14	   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
15	3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
16	4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
17	   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
18	   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
19	5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
20	6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
21	   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
22	   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
23	7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
24	   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
25	   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
26	8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
27	9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
28	   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
29	10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).
30	
31	PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:
32	
33	````markdown
34	## What changed
35	- <what the product can now do>
36	
37	## How verified
38	- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
39	```
40	<tail of ./hq check>
41	```
42	
43	## Risks
44	- <what could break, or "none">
45	
46	## Screenshots
47	<UI changes only, else "n/a">
48	````
49	
50	Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
51	`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
52	`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
53	`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
54	Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.
55	
56	Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
57	`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
58	
59	Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
60	with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).
61

### Goal

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] City screen uses `lib/map` to show one Mapbox point layer per sensor, shaded by server-provided indicative % highly sleep disturbed, with a readable legend.

- [ ] Selecting a sensor highlights its marker and linked list row, showing source, 30-night Lnight, nights, last update and any clamping with the label "indicative road-traffic estimate, WHO curve".
- [ ] The feature exports its sensor overlay through `apps/mobile/src/features/city/index.ts` so Quiet Stays can highlight score sources without importing private components.
- [ ] An unavailable API falls back to the shared fixture with an explicit sample/simulated-data label; web and iOS give equivalent selection and details.

The library doesn't give me per-feature shading, and I can't change it, so I'm weighing options within the MapView alone. Without shading there, map markers would all be the same ink color, with only the selected one highlighted. The shading would then have to live in the list rows and a legend instead, which falls short of the requirement that the shading appear on the map itself.

I'm settling on building the full feature with a `shade` property on each point, so a future library change can pick it up, and filing a platform follow-up for data-driven point colour. I'll flag the gap in my report rather than treating it as a blocker. Next I'm laying out the city feature modules, starting with the pure sensor-state logic that separates shaded, not-enough, out-of-range and stale readings.

I'm checking the fixture's timestamps next, since they decide whether stale readings would be the whole dataset, and then I'll set the shade bands and the overlay export from what the data actually looks like.

I'm exporting the sensor overlay in a few forms, a `sensorMapFeatures` helper plus a `SensorMap` component and `useCitySensors` hook, so Quiet Stays can highlight its score sources. Next I want to look at the fixture and the UI components, and check how the night screen falls back when there's no data.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/nick/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/tripoli/.claude/skills/anti-slop

If `.ux-profile.md` exists at the project root, read it before changing layout, color, or type.

### Intent

AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.

### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)

- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.

### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles

- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.
- If it appears in a generic SaaS landing template, assume it is slop until proven functional.
- Cross-check `.ux-profile.md` banned list — it may extend these rules.

### Concrete Scenarios (Before vs. After)

#### ❌ Anti-Pattern

Sign-up uses a `conic-gradient` "Get Started" button. Login form inputs each have a leading gray icon. Empty project view shows a cartoon character high-fiving. Settings show "Last updated" inside a lavender pill. A modal uses `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` with no border on a busy background.

#### ✅ Best Practice

Primary CTA is solid accent fill. Search field keeps one magnifier icon; other fields are label + input only. Empty state: heading, one sentence of value, "Create project" button, optional simple 24px monochrome icon. Metadata runs as 12px secondary text. Modal uses opaque L3 surface, 1px border, optional scrim — no blur.

### Framework-Agnostic Implementation Blueprint

**Audit pass (grep / search changed files):**

```
backdrop-filter
conic-gradient
linear-gradient.*(#.*,#.*,#)   /* multi-hue gradients on buttons */
illustration|empty-state.*svg  /* review for cartoon people */
border-radius: 999             /* pill wrappers on static text */
```

**Replace patterns:**

```css
/* ❌ Slop */
.btn-primary {
  background: conic-gradient(from 180deg, #f00, #ff0, #0f0, #00f, #f0f);
}
.panel {
  backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}

/* ✅ Restrained */
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
}
.panel {
  background: var(--surface-l3);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-l2);
}
```

Use [reference/slop-checklist.md](reference/slop-checklist.md) for the full identification matrix.

### Agent Checklist

- [ ] Read `.ux-profile.md` if present; merge its ban list with this skill.
- [ ] Scan CTAs — no rainbow or multi-hue radial gradients.
- [ ] Scan overlays — no unbounded glassmorphism; border + opaque fallback if blur exists.
- [ ] Scan empty states — no cartoon people illustrations.
- [ ] Scan inputs — icons only where functional (search, clear, toggle).
- [ ] Scan metadata — no decorative pill wrappers on static text.
- [ ] After a slop pass: list frame, row dividers, and search chrome still present — an empty-looking table is a fail.
- [ ] Run slop checklist matrix on any AI-generated or imported component.
